title: Write all terms in base $$3$$.
text:
$$3**{2x-3}+9**{x-1}=27**{x-2}$$ 
 Notice that the bases and exponents are different. But all bases are powers of $$3$$, so we can write everything in terms of base $$3$$. 

$$3**{2x-3}+(3**2)**{x-1}=(3**3)**{x-2}$$

title: Apply the laws of exponentiation for powers
LHS Pull out a factor of $$3**{2x-3}$$
text: There is no exponential rule for sums of exponential expressions. To combine the two terms on the left-hand side, we look for a common factor. Observe that $$3**{2(x-1)}=3**{2x-2}=3**{2x-3+1}=3**{2x-3}\cdot $$3.$$

title: Carry out the previous step
text: Rewrite the left hand side as \n $$3**{2x-3}+3**{2(x-1)}=3**{2x-3}(1+3)$$

title: Put it together
text: Plugging this into the left-hand side of the equation, we get \n $$3**{2x-3}(1+3)=3**{3(x-2)}$$

title: Apply the laws of logarithms
text:
Apply the law of logarithms for products to the left-hand side so that 
 $$\log_3(3**{2x-3}(4))=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)})$$ 
 becomes 
 $$\log_3(3**{2x-3})+\log_3(4)=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)})$$

title: Apply the cancellation principle
text:
Log base $$3$$ undoes exponentiation with base $$3$$. So the equation reduces to 

$$\log_3(3**{2x-3})+\log_3(4)=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)}),$$ which becomes 

$$2x-3+\log_3(4)=3(x-2)$$.
